sealed.statement: High-volume playback snapshot evidence is streamed to gzip at capture time, and every supported snapshot reader transparently accepts both legacy plain and compressed artifacts without changing replay semantics.

constraints.statement: After explicit declaration and before first execution, record an independent approving design-review receipt bound to the sealed declaration.
If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.
Snapshot gzip is streamed during capture, fully finalized before manifest publication, and leaves no authoritative plain sibling or partial-success manifest.
Supported readers prefer an explicitly requested existing artifact and otherwise resolve its gzip sibling, preserving legacy plain inputs, diagnostics, and replay results.

claim: Pre-edit harness guardrail baseline is green: file-size ratchet 28/28 source and 21/21 test; scoped metrics report 18 inherited cyclomatic and 4 inherited cognitive violations across five existing reader/writer files; literal audit has zero new violations and 32 inherited baseline entries.

Independent design review rejected the initial gzip plan because it omitted browser/admin/census consumers, did not preserve live-follow readability, allowed storage failures to be swallowed as topology warnings, and left stale plain/manifest precedence and full stream finalization underspecified.
rulesOut: ordinary open gzip stream plus four-reader-only compatibility sweep

claim: Independent corrected-design review rejected changing the admin logical path to an explicit gzip suffix and placing shared codec ownership under test/: both would break legacy archive or packaged-runtime compatibility. The final design keeps logical snapshots.ndjson paths and moves the shared resolver/codec into neutral published src/diagnostics ownership.
rulesOut: explicit-gzip admin defaults and src-to-test shared helper import

claim: Independent adversarial design review approved the single published codec/resolver owner, serialized sync-flushed capture, fail-closed recorder lifecycle, logical admin compatibility, active complete-record streaming, and exhaustive reader parity bar.

Independent adversarial implementation review first rejected the shared decoded read stream for leaking the source file descriptor on consumer abort, then approved the corrected diff after backward close propagation was added and a multi-chunk incompressible-payload regression test was shown to fail without the fix; resolver precedence, writer ordering and latching, recorder fail-closed manifest handling, admin strict/incomplete gating, five-family consumer parity, and viewer byte-identity all held under attack.

note: Frame check: the goal (compressed playback evidence with universal reader compatibility) is correct and the implementation is independently verified, but the Quest frame itself is wrong — its sealed solve/epics citation pins workflow scope while every owned path is runtime, so no attempt on this frame can ever be admitted. The right altitude is to keep the verified design and evidence and re-house them in a runtime-scoped sibling declaration rather than fight the scope guard.

reason: Mis-scoped at authoring: the sealed links cite solve/epics/convergence-loop-and-workflow-overhead.md, which classifies the Quest as workflow scope, while the sealed goal owns runtime paths (src/diagnostics, src/admin, test/distributed harness); the runtime change artifact is permanently inadmissible under the scope-cross guard and class-correction to product is lint-blocked by the oracle doneWhen probe. Superseded by a runtime-scoped sibling Quest carrying the same design, findings, and verified implementation.
